newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar gains U.S. cent on bank rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar gains U.S. cent on bank rate hike.

text.p: The Canadian dollar shot up one U.S. cent in heavy trading on Thursday after the Bank of Canada unexpectedly raised its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent.
The Canadian dollar was trading at C$1.3765 (US$72.64) following the rate hike after opening this morning at $1.3960 (US$0.7163).

The sharp rise of the Canada unit halted a two-week slide against the U.S. dollar, which was capped on Wednesday by repeated Bank of Canada intervention to buy Canada dollars and prop up the currency.
Before Thursday's rate hike, traders had predicted the Canadian dollar would break through support at C$1.3975 (US$0.7155) and touch the key C$1.4000 (US$0.7142) level.

"It was a total surprise to us because we started the day telling our clients that we would probably see the previous high of April 18 of C$1.4024 (US$0.7130) this week," said a trader with one of Canada's largest banks.
"This move in the light of a 25 basis-point-hike has been incredibly dramatic. We've seen easings, we've seen tightenings, but they're usually not this violent," the trader said.
The central bank said in a statement following the move that the rate hike was designed to "counter excessive easing in monetary conditions and to provide support for the currency."
In May, the central bank said publicly that the need for a stimulative monetary policy had disappeared and that the bank would move toward a more neutral position.
The gradual erosion of the Canadian dollar in June, however, placed even greater pressure on the Bank to make a pre-emptive strike on interest rates.

"This move is designed to offset the implied easing in monetary conditions at a time when it looks like economic activity is starting to pick up on a sustained basis," said Paul Ferley, assistant chief economist with the Bank of Montreal.
"With this hike, the Bank has made it clear that it is in a position to raise rates irrespective of what the Fed does," Ferley added.
The U.S. Federal Reserve will meet on July 1-2 to decide whether a surge in U.S. economic activity in the second quarter warrants another interest rate hike.
The Fed last raised its federal funds rate by 25 basis points on March 25, a move that touched off a U.S. dollar rally and a slide in the value of the Canadian dollar.
Analysts said that the Bank of Canada's rate hike positions the Canadian dollar to benefit further if the Fed decides to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged next week.
Ferley said Canada's strong economic fundamentals could begin to underpin a sustained Canada dollar rally and take the currency to C$1.3700 (US$0.7299) in the next month.
